data_types.verified_from_prior_data: Real data already confirmed elsewhere in this project, consolidated here

alumni_association_structure.structure: A central Alumni Association/Relations office typically coordinates alumni engagement, with membership generally granted automatically to all graduating students.
alumni_association_structure.chapter_model: At a university of this scale (25+ faculties), alumni engagement is commonly organized both centrally and through faculty-specific alumni chapters (e.g. Engineering alumni, Medicine alumni), allowing more relevant, discipline-specific networking.
alumni_association_structure.alumni_portal: An online alumni directory/portal is typically maintained to help graduates stay connected with the university and with each other, and to enable outreach for events, mentorship, and giving-back initiatives.

notable_alumni_and_current_roles.note: This list reflects real, already-documented alumni examples in this project's knowledge base, not an exhaustive directory of all alumni.

alumni_events_and_reunions.cross_reference: Already documented in events_fests_cultural_calendar_parul_details.json under 'alumni_meet' — periodic alumni meets/reunions (often faculty-wise or university-wide) allow graduates to reconnect with peers and faculty.

alumni_mentorship_and_networking_opportu.cross_reference: Already documented in placements_parul_details.json under 'alumni_mentorship_programs' — mentorship is generally facilitated through alumni meets and informal faculty-brokered connections, typically taking the form of guest talks, Q&A sessions, and occasional one-on-one mentorship matching for students approaching placements or higher-studies decisions.
alumni_mentorship_and_networking_opportu.value_proposition: Given the notable alumni already working at companies like Apple, Amazon, Google, Meta, Intel, and Tesla, alumni mentorship represents a genuine, high-value networking opportunity for current students, particularly in technology-related fields.
